exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Funding model: currency reservation with haircut, cash sleeve, or pool buffer; and the percentage-grant fixing point.
original_provisional_answer: Reservation against capacity computed in the same transaction. Grant states Reserved → FundingPlanned → Funded before payment. Each pool keeps a cash liquidity buffer (sponsor-set percentage, default 2% of pool value) so routine grants fund from cash without per-grant trades. Percentage grants fix their amount at approval.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: GAAP requires NFPs to disclose qualitative and quantitative information on financial assets available for general expenditure within one year, considering donor, legal, contractual and internal board limits; it prescribes no liquidity buffer level.

Fidelity Charitable discloses $77.3B of financial assets available within one year (of ~$85.9B net assets) and treats Level 3, NAV-measured and PIF assets as unavailable; it discloses no fixed cash-buffer percentage.
No statute, regulation or accounting standard found prescribes a per-pool cash buffer percentage (e.g. 2%) for DAF sponsors; the 2% default is a business assumption.
Grant expense/payable is recognized at a measured amount when the unconditional promise is made (720-25-25-1); a percentage grant therefore needs a fixed amount at its recognition point.

supporting_interpretation: Atomic capacity reservation plus explicit funding states prevents over-commitment; a pool-level cash sleeve lets routine grants settle without per-grant trades. Fixing a percentage grant's amount at approval aligns the reservation, the expense measurement and the donor-visible amount.
competing_interpretation: A fixed 2% buffer may be too small in December peaks or for illiquid pools and too large (cash drag) for steady pools; some sponsors liquidate per grant (Fidelity sells contributed property and pools carry cash per investment objective). A percentage could instead be fixed at payment (donor expectation of 'x% of balance at payment').
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound configures the buffer and state machine; the sponsor's investment committee owns the buffer level as investment/liquidity policy. Unbound must not ship 2% as an unlabeled default.
business_assumptions: Grant outflows are forecastable from history by pool and season
Pools hold daily-liquid securities except designated illiquid sleeves
Sponsor's investment policy statement permits a cash sleeve
recommended_answer: Keep atomic reservation in the same transaction and Reserved -> FundingPlanned -> Funded. Replace the fixed 2% default with a sponsor-set buffer per pool calibrated from a stress model (e.g. high-percentile net outflow over the settlement horizon plus December peak), with 2% allowed only as an explicitly labeled placeholder until 12 months of data exist. Fix percentage grants at approval (the amount that is reserved, communicated and expensed), with an option to re-fix only by a new approval.
remaining_uncertainty: Actual outflow distributions per sponsor/pool; whether any sponsor IPS forbids cash sleeves; donor expectation for percentage grants.
consequences_if_wrong: Buffer too small: grant payment delays and forced intraday sales; too large: cash drag on donor accounts and investment-policy deviation.
conservative_fallback: Per-grant liquidation with T+settlement funding when the buffer is breached; block the grant at FundingPlanned until cash settles.
alternative_design: (a) Fixed % buffer: low cost, simple, but miscalibrated (exposure: payment delays/cash drag). (b) Stress-calibrated buffer (recommended): modest analytics cost, low friction, low exposure. (c) Per-grant liquidation: no cash drag but trade cost, settlement delay and ops friction; loses same-day grant payment.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given two concurrent grant approvals that together exceed fund capacity, when both commit, then exactly one succeeds and the other is rejected with no over-reservation.

Given a pool with buffer policy version v, when buffer cash falls below the configured floor, then a replenishment trade instruction is generated and an alert raised, and the policy version is recorded on the event.
Given a percentage grant of 10% approved when fund value is $50,000, when market value changes before payment, then the payable remains $5,000.
Given no stress calibration exists for a pool, when the buffer default is displayed, then it is labeled 'placeholder - not calibrated'.
reconsideration_triggers: Two or more buffer breaches in a quarter
external_authorization_required: Sponsor investment committee (or board) approval of the liquidity/buffer policy within the investment policy statement.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: States a default 2% buffer without evidence; no authority or audited sponsor disclosure supports a universal 2%.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Make buffer sponsor-set and stress-calibrated; label any 2% value as an uncalibrated placeholder.

landscape_update_candidates: Fidelity Charitable FY2025 liquidity disclosure: $77.3B financial assets available within one year; Level 3/NAV/PIF assets treated as unavailable.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Fee base and posting: on what value, when, net of what, and payable to whom?
original_provisional_answer: Fee base is end-of-day fund market value, including reserved but unpaid amounts and excluding fees embedded in pool NAV. Fees accrue daily (actual/365) and settle monthly, with no fee on accrued fees. Minimum fees apply per sponsor schedule. Fees are recognized as sponsor revenue when settled.
relevant_requirements: unbound:requirements/accounting/CANONICAL-CHART-AND-POSTING-RULES.md §4 matrix row 'Sponsor fee assessed to a DAF'
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Fidelity Charitable charges 0.60% of average Giving Account assets (or $100 minimum); for pools the fee is charged to the pool pro rata daily and affects NAV; for assets not in pools (including contributed property not yet sold) the fee is charged directly to the account.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Fees and Expenses - General operating expenses

authoritative_findings.claim: Vanguard Charitable's 0.60% fee accrues daily, reduces pool NAV and is presented as 'Net Assets Released for Administrative Fee' used to pay operating expenses - i.e. an internal release within the same entity, not third-party revenue.
The Boston Foundation funds operations by administrative fees 'allocated from other fund categories based upon those funds' market value' - an internal allocation.
Foundation for the Carolinas reports 'Administrative fees received' of $7.0M as revenue on $4.4B of net assets and recognizes fees in the fiscal year in which they occur (accrual), not when settled.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Statement of Activities; Note 2 Administrative Fees Received

authoritative_findings.claim: Internal fees charged by a sponsor to its own DAFs within the same legal entity are not revenue from an external party and are eliminated/presented as internal transfers on the entity's GAAP statements; fees from agency funds (liabilities) or other entities can be revenue.

supporting_interpretation: Daily accrual on end-of-day market value, monthly settlement and no fee-on-fee is consistent with Fidelity/Vanguard practice (daily NAV-based accrual). Excluding fees embedded in pool NAV avoids double charging.
competing_interpretation: Fee base could be average assets (Fidelity), quarterly balance (Boston DAFs), or 8-quarter average (Boston endowments). Including reserved-but-unpaid grants in the base is a pricing choice; including recognized grants payable is not, because those amounts are already expensed and no longer fund net assets.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound must support multiple versioned fee bases and day-count conventions and must post internal fees as interfund transfers with consolidated elimination, recognizing revenue only for fees from external payers (agency funds, partner invoices) on an accrual basis.
business_assumptions: Sponsor contracts define fee schedules
Some sponsors host agency/pass-through funds whose fees are external revenue
recommended_answer: Version the fee basis per schedule (end-of-day market value default; average-balance and periodic-balance options), day count, accrual and settlement cadence, minimum, and payer source. Exclude grants already recognized as payable from the base; reserved-but-uncommunicated amounts are included by default (still fund net assets) and configurable. No fee on accrued fees; exclude fees embedded in pool NAV. Accounting: fees charged to the sponsor's own DAFs are internal transfers (fund-level expense / operating-fund recovery) eliminated in entity statements; fees from agency funds or other external payers are revenue recognized as the service period elapses (accrual), not on settlement.
remaining_uncertainty: Each sponsor auditor's presentation choice (gross internal fee lines vs net release); ASC 606 analysis for external fee revenue was not researched in depth.
consequences_if_wrong: Recognizing internal fees as revenue overstates revenue and expense; cash-basis recognition misstates period results.
conservative_fallback: Post internal fees only as fund-dimension transfers with a zero entity-level P&L effect; treat external fee revenue on accrual with CPA review.
alternative_design: (a) Single hard-coded base: cheapest, but fails sponsor contracts. (b) Versioned FeeBase contract (recommended): moderate build, low exposure. (c) Delegate fee calc to custodian NAV only: no platform calc, but loses per-account minimums/tiers and fund-level transparency.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given a DAF with fees charged by its own sponsor, when entity-level statements are generated, then fee entries net to zero across funds (eliminated) and no revenue line is produced.
Given an agency fund charged a fee for March, when March closes unpaid, then fee revenue and a receivable are recognized in March.
Given a grant recognized as payable, when the daily fee base is computed, then the payable amount is excluded.
Given a fee schedule change effective on date D, when fees are computed across D, then each day uses the version in force that day.
reconsideration_triggers: New fee type with external payer
external_authorization_required: Executed sponsor fee schedule / program terms; sponsor controller-approved fee accounting policy.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: 'Fees are recognized as sponsor revenue when settled' conflicts with GAAP accrual and with audited practice: internal DAF fees are internal releases/transfers (Vanguard Note 7; Boston allocations), and FFTC recognizes fees in the year they occur.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Internal fees: interfund transfer, eliminated; external fees: revenue on accrual over the service period.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: Including amounts already recognized as grants payable would charge fees on assets no longer in fund net assets.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Distinguish reserved (included, configurable) from recognized payable (excluded).

landscape_update_candidates: Vanguard Charitable presents its DAF administrative fee as 'net assets released' (FY2025 Note 7), not revenue.
FFTC FY2025 reports only $7.0M administrative fee revenue on $4.4B net assets, suggesting internal fees eliminated.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Contribution valuation, completed-gift dates, acknowledgment timing and returned contributions.
original_provisional_answer: Contributions credit grantable capacity only on Final: ACH after the sponsor-set return window (default 5 business days); wire on receipt; check on clear; securities on settlement into custody. Acknowledgment is issued on CompletedGiftDetermined ∧ SponsorAccepted. Accepted assets never return to a donor; returned grant funds go back to the originating fund.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: A contribution is ordinarily made when delivery is effected; a mailed check that clears in due course is made on the mailing date.

An endorsed stock certificate is completed on delivery/mailing to the donee; if delivered to the donor's bank/broker or issuer for transfer, the gift is complete when transferred on the corporation's books.
Credit card gifts are deductible in the year charged; pay-by-phone gifts are delivered on the date the financial institution pays.

DAF contributions are deductible only with a CWA from the sponsor stating it has exclusive legal control; CWAs for >=$250 must state cash amount and describe (not value) noncash property, and be obtained by the earlier of the filing date or due date.
Donor tax FMV of traded securities is the mean of high and low selling prices on the valuation date - distinct from GAAP fair value used by the sponsor.
Fidelity treats EFT contributions as timely if initiated by Dec 31 and wires/securities if received by Dec 31 (guidelines).
Fidelity records contributions on the date received and accepted; property not accepted is returned; accepted contributions are irrevocable and non-refundable.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Note 2 Donor Contributions; EV-B-007 Contributions - General

authoritative_findings.claim: ACH consumer debit return windows extend to 60 days for some return reasons (R11; R10 by rule), so a 5-business-day hold is a risk-based availability rule, not finality.

supporting_interpretation: Gift completion (tax date), GAAP recognition (received/accepted), availability for granting (risk of reversal) and acknowledgment are four separate facts. For donor-initiated ACH (credit from donor bank or sponsor-pulled debit) no regulation fixes the date; by analogy to pay-by-phone, the gift is made when the donor's bank pays (settlement), with initiation date shown as a sponsor guideline (Fidelity). Card: date charged.
competing_interpretation: Some practitioners treat ACH debit gifts as made on the authorization/initiation date (Fidelity's year-end guideline) - a donor-favorable reading not confirmed by regulation. Electronic DTC securities transfers: date received in the sponsor's account (books-transfer analog) vs date donor instructed.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound records the facts and dates and applies sponsor rule tables; the sponsor issues the CWA and owns the completed-gift rule. CWA must not state a value for noncash property (only description), though sponsors may show a non-tax informational value clearly labeled.
business_assumptions: Sponsor accepts ACH, wire, check, card, DTC securities
Sponsor reserves acceptance discretion (as Fidelity)
recommended_answer: Store separately: GiftCompletionDate (tax: check=mailing/postmark date if cleared; certificate=delivery/mailing; broker/DTC=date credited to sponsor account; card=charge date; ACH=settlement date with initiation date retained; wire=receipt), AcceptanceDate (GAAP recognition), AvailabilityDate (sponsor risk rule: e.g. ACH default 5 business days configurable, card per dispute risk; explicitly not finality), and AcknowledgmentDate (issued after acceptance; noncash described without value). If an ACH/card payment is later returned or charged back, reverse the contribution (it was never completed) and void/amend the acknowledgment; this is not a 'refund' of an accepted asset. Accepted assets are never refunded to donors; returned grant funds go back to the originating fund.
remaining_uncertainty: No IRS guidance explicitly fixes the gift date for ACH debits or DTC transfers; card-network dispute windows not verified here.
consequences_if_wrong: Wrong tax year on acknowledgments (donor deduction disallowed or amended), grants funded from reversed money.
conservative_fallback: Acknowledge using settlement/receipt date; keep capacity unavailable until the sponsor's risk window passes; flag Dec 31/Jan 1 boundary items for manual review.
alternative_design: (a) Single 'Final' date (original): simple but conflates tax date with availability (high exposure on year-end). (b) Four-date model (recommended): small schema cost, low exposure. (c) Accept only wires/DTC for large gifts: removes reversal risk but adds donor friction and loses card/ACH gifts.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given a check postmarked Dec 31 and deposited Jan 3 that clears, when the acknowledgment is generated, then the gift date is Dec 31.
Given DTC shares credited to the sponsor account on Jan 2 after a Dec 30 instruction, when acknowledged, then the gift date is Jan 2 and the instruction date is retained.
Given an ACH gift returned R10 on day 40, when the return posts, then the contribution and capacity are reversed and the acknowledgment is voided or amended.
Given a noncash gift >= $250, when the CWA is generated, then it describes the property without stating a tax value and states exclusive legal control.
reconsideration_triggers: IRS guidance on electronic contribution dates
external_authorization_required: Sponsor counsel/CPA sign-off of the completed-gift rule table and acknowledgment template (sponsor is the legal issuer).

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: 'ACH final after 5 business days' treats a risk hold as finality; ACH consumer returns can arrive up to 60 days.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Name it AvailabilityDate (risk rule), separate from GiftCompletionDate and Final.

corrections_to_prior_records.record_or_artifact: RCD-019 'Accepted assets never return to a donor'
corrections_to_prior_records.issue: A returned/charged-back payment is not an accepted asset being refunded; the contribution never completed.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Model reversal of incomplete contributions distinctly from (prohibited) refunds.

landscape_update_candidates: Fidelity Charitable year-end guideline uses EFT initiation date and receipt date for wires/securities.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Reconciliation: break-blocking thresholds and owners, attestation versus auto-pass, omnibus allocation method.
original_provisional_answer: Continuous automated reconciliation. Routine matched items auto-pass. Independent sampled attestation of at least 5% of passes per month. Any unexplained cash break blocks statement publication for the affected funds. Security price breaks follow the sponsor tolerance. Allocation method is declared per custody account. Fund and restriction are balancing segments.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Exclusive reliance on any percentage or numerical materiality threshold has no basis in the accounting literature or the law; qualitative factors matter.
Audit planning materiality for NFPs is a judgment; ISA 320 gives 1% of total revenue or expenses as an example, with higher or lower percentages possible.
No authoritative source found prescribes a 5% attestation sample of automated reconciliations; sample sizes are a control-design choice.

supporting_interpretation: Continuous automated matching with auto-pass for exact matches and independent review on a risk-based sample is consistent with modern control design; blocking statement publication for affected funds on unexplained cash breaks protects donors.
competing_interpretation: Some controllers will require full monthly sign-off of bank/custody reconciliations by a named preparer and reviewer regardless of automation; auditors may test the automated control's design and operation instead of samples.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound provides tolerances, sampling engine and blocking; sponsor controller sets thresholds and sample rates. Materiality for statement-blocking must be per sponsor, with absolute and relative components, plus zero tolerance for unexplained cash breaks on affected funds.
business_assumptions: Daily bank/custody feeds available
Controller exists at each sponsor
recommended_answer: Continuous reconciliation; exact matches auto-pass; independent attestation of a risk-stratified sample whose size is set by the controller (statistically or judgmentally, with increased sampling after errors) - 5% is not a requirement and must be labeled a configurable starting value. Unexplained cash breaks block statements only for affected funds; security price/position tolerances absolute+relative per asset class. Monthly controller sign-off on reconciliation completeness. Allocation method declared per custody account; fund and restriction as balancing segments.
remaining_uncertainty: Sponsor auditor expectations for reliance on automated controls (SOC 1 of Unbound may be needed).
consequences_if_wrong: Too lax: undetected misstatement; too strict: blocked statements and ops cost.
conservative_fallback: Monthly preparer/reviewer sign-off of every account reconciliation in addition to automation.
alternative_design: (a) Attest every reconciliation: high labor, low exposure. (b) Risk-based sampling + automated control evidence + SOC 1 (recommended): moderate cost, lets auditors rely on controls. (c) Auto-pass only: lowest cost, high exposure.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given an unexplained cash break of any amount in fund F, when statements are generated, then F's statement is blocked and others publish.

Given controller sets sample rate r and stratum weights, when month closes, then the sample drawn is reproducible from a seed and attested items recorded with reviewer identity independent from the preparer.
Given an error found in the sample, when next month's sample is drawn, then the rate for that stratum increases per policy.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: 'at least 5% of passes per month' presented as a decided minimum with no authority.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Make sample rate controller-set and risk-based; label 5% as configurable starting value.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Must every NAV have a human checker?
original_provisional_answer: In-tolerance NAVs are published by deterministic policy (A3) under sponsor delegation, with a sampled human review the next business day. Out-of-tolerance NAVs need a human approver (A4).
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Charitable organizations and pooled funds they maintain for charitable assets are excluded from the Investment Company Act definition of investment company, so registered-fund NAV rules do not govern DAF pools.

For registered funds, Rule 2a-5 requires a board or valuation designee to assess valuation risk, apply and test methodologies and oversee pricing services - it does not require a human checker per NAV; it is a useful analog only.
Fidelity Charitable values investments using independent pricing services approved by the Trustees.

supporting_interpretation: Deterministic publication of in-tolerance NAVs under a documented delegation, with exceptions (stale/missing prices, tolerance breaches, corporate actions) to a human approver and a risk-based after-the-fact sample, matches the Rule 2a-5 oversight model.
competing_interpretation: Some sponsors' investment committees may require daily human sign-off; auditors may prefer it when pricing feeds are from a single vendor.
applicability_to_unbound: Applies to Unbound pool NAV publishing; delegation must be recorded per sponsor.
business_assumptions: Independent pricing vendors
Tolerance rules defined per asset class
recommended_answer: No law or standard requires a human checker for every NAV. Publish in-tolerance NAVs by deterministic policy under a recorded investment-committee delegation; route out-of-tolerance, stale, missing or manually overridden prices to a human approver before publication; perform a risk-based next-business-day independent sample; block affected publication on unresolved breaks; review the delegation and tolerances at least annually.
consequences_if_wrong: Mispriced NAV affects fees, grants and donor statements; correction requires reprocessing.
conservative_fallback: Human approval of every NAV until the delegation is executed.
alternative_design: (a) Human checks all NAVs: daily labor, low exposure. (b) Delegated deterministic publication + exceptions (recommended). (c) Custodian-published NAV only: removes Unbound valuation exposure but depends on custodian SLAs.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given no recorded delegation for sponsor S, when a NAV is computed, then it requires human approval.
Given a price older than the staleness limit, when NAV computes, then publication is blocked and an exception created.
Given an in-tolerance NAV, when published automatically, then the policy version and inputs are stored and eligible for sampling.
external_authorization_required: Sponsor investment committee/board resolution delegating NAV publication and approving tolerances and pricing sources.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Minimum fee versus reserved grant capacity (OD-10)
original_provisional_answer: Reserved grants always take priority. A fee shortfall is carried as a receivable against future capacity, waivable by A4. It never draws reserved capacity.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Fidelity charges a $100 minimum annual fee; where 0.60% is below $100 the difference is assessed at fiscal year end, prorated for accounts funded during the year.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Fees and Expenses - General operating expenses

authoritative_findings.claim: Donors have no legal or beneficial interest in DAF sub-accounts; all assets are the sponsor's.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Note 2 Net Assets Without Donor Restrictions

authoritative_findings.claim: A grant becomes a liability (payable) only when an unconditional promise is made; a reservation not yet communicated is an internal earmark, not a liability.

supporting_interpretation: Because the sponsor owns all assets, priority between internal fees and reserved grants is sponsor policy. Communicated/recognized grants are liabilities and must rank ahead of internal fees; uncommunicated reservations can also be protected by policy to keep donor-facing commitments.
competing_interpretation: Fee-first ensures the operating fund is paid; a 'receivable' from a DAF with no balance is not an asset in entity GAAP statements (internal) and may never be collected.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound implements priority, shortfall tracking and waiver workflow; the sponsor sets policy.
business_assumptions: Minimum fees exist in sponsor schedules
recommended_answer: Recognized grants payable always rank ahead of fees; reserved (uncommunicated) grants also rank ahead by default policy. A fee shortfall is tracked as a fund-level memo/interfund claim against future capacity (not an entity-level asset), waivable by an authorized approver with reason; collect from the next available capacity; write off on fund closure.
remaining_uncertainty: Sponsor program terms may give fees priority; auditor view on interfund receivable presentation.
consequences_if_wrong: Grant failure for donor-communicated commitments or uncollected fees.
conservative_fallback: Block new reservations when projected fees exceed residual capacity.
alternative_design: (a) Fee-first: protects operating revenue, risks grant failure. (b) Grants-first with memo claim (recommended). (c) Assess minimum fee only at year end (Fidelity model): simplest, shortfall rarely arises intra-year.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given a fund with $50 free capacity, $200 reserved and $100 minimum fee due, when fees assess, then $50 is charged, $50 recorded as fee claim, and the reservation is untouched.
Given a waiver by an authorized approver, when recorded, then the claim is cleared with reason and approver identity.
Given entity-level statements, when generated, then fee claims are eliminated and not presented as receivables from third parties.
external_authorization_required: Sponsor program terms/fee schedule stating priority and waiver authority.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: An intra-entity fee shortfall is not a receivable on the sponsor's GAAP statements.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Call it a fund-level fee claim (memo/interfund), eliminated at entity level.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Which GrantRecognitionPoint values are permitted?
original_provisional_answer: Permitted GrantRecognitionPoint values: ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee (default) and PaymentReleased (only where payment is the first communication to the grantee). SponsorApproval is NOT a selectable policy; it collapses into ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee when the approval notice is sent in the same period. Conditional grants (barrier plus right of return/release) are recognized when the barrier is overcome.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Contributions made are expensed in the period made; unconditional promises to give cash are recognized as payables and contribution expense.
A donor-imposed condition requires a barrier and a right of return/release; ambiguous stipulations are presumed conditional; conditional promises are not recognized until the barrier is overcome.

Pre-2018 Codification text (958-720-25-2, superseded by ASU 2018-08) said an unconditional promise is recognized when the donor has an obligation, which 'generally occurs when the donor approves a specific grant or when the recipient of the promise is notified'; donor-reserved rescission rights prevented recognition.

Audited sponsor practice recognizes unconditional grants when approved: Colorado Gives ('when they are approved'), Boston Foundation ('when approved by the Board or committed to grantees'), FFTC ('when approved and all conditions have been met'), Vanguard (expense when authorized).
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Note 2 Grants (also EV-B-011 (i), EV-B-012 Note 9, EV-B-009 Note 2)

authoritative_findings.claim: A promise to give is an agreement; recognition requires verifiable documentation that the promise was made and received, implying communication to the recipient.

supporting_interpretation: Requiring communication prevents expensing internal approvals that the sponsor can still freely cancel; Unbound sends the notice at approval, so approval and communication fall in the same period in normal operation.
competing_interpretation: The removed Codification text and current audited practice accept approval as the recognition event where the sponsor's approval creates an obligation; DAF sponsors approve grants for payment within days and rarely rescind. Removing SponsorApproval as a selectable policy contradicts majority audited practice.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound must not hard-code an accounting policy that differs from sponsors' audited policies; it must capture approval, communication, conditions and rescission rights independently and let the sponsor's policy choose the trigger.
business_assumptions: Unbound auto-sends approval notices
Sponsors retain the right to cancel before payment in program terms
recommended_answer: Permitted values: SponsorApproval (allowed where the sponsor's CPA-documented policy treats approval as creating the obligation and the sponsor does not reserve a free rescission right), ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee (platform default), PaymentReleased (only where payment is the first communication). Conditional grants recognized when the barrier is overcome. Always capture approval, communication, condition and rescission evidence; produce a period-end cutoff report of approved-but-uncommunicated items.
remaining_uncertainty: Current Codification wording of 958-605/958-405/958-720 on recognition timing not read (paywalled); auditor positions vary.
consequences_if_wrong: Expense/payable cutoff misstatements at year end (usually small because approval-to-payment is days).
conservative_fallback: Default ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee with same-moment notification, eliminating the timing difference.
alternative_design: (a) Single fixed trigger: simple but conflicts with some audited policies. (b) Policy enumeration with evidence capture (recommended). (c) Make approval and notification atomic so the choice is immaterial: low cost, removes most exposure; loses only deferred-notice workflows.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given policy ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee and a grant approved Dec 31 with notice sent Jan 2, when Dec closes, then no expense is recognized in Dec and the item appears on the cutoff report.
Given policy SponsorApproval without CPA policy evidence attached, when a sponsor tries to activate it, then activation is blocked.
Given a grant with a measurable barrier and right of release, when approved, then no expense is recognized until the barrier is recorded as met.
external_authorization_required: Sponsor management's written grant-recognition accounting policy, accepted by the sponsor's external auditor in the first audited year.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: Rests on 'promise requires communication' cited as secondary knowledge with the Codification unread; superseded 958-720-25-2 expressly allowed approval OR notification and four audited sponsors recognize at approval.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Restore SponsorApproval as a selectable, evidence-gated policy; keep communicated as default.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: Cites ASC 720-25-25-1 as establishing communication; the paragraph only says period made and payables for unconditional promises.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Cite 720-25-25-1 for measurement/period only; communication is interpretation.

landscape_update_candidates: Grant recognition policies in FY2025 audits: Colorado Gives, Boston Foundation, FFTC, Vanguard Charitable all recognize at approval/authorization.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Which GrantRecognitionPoint does each sponsor adopt, and does approval without notice to the charity create a promise to give?
original_provisional_answer: Default recognition point for every sponsor is ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee; the platform sends the approval notice automatically on approval, so in normal operation expense, payable and approval fall in the same period. Approval without notice does not create a promise to give.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Contributions made are expensed in the period made; unconditional promises to give cash are recognized as payables and contribution expense.
A donor-imposed condition requires a barrier and a right of return/release; ambiguous stipulations are presumed conditional; conditional promises are not recognized until the barrier is overcome.

Pre-2018 Codification text (958-720-25-2, superseded by ASU 2018-08) said an unconditional promise is recognized when the donor has an obligation, which 'generally occurs when the donor approves a specific grant or when the recipient of the promise is notified'; donor-reserved rescission rights prevented recognition.

Audited sponsor practice recognizes unconditional grants when approved: Colorado Gives ('when they are approved'), Boston Foundation ('when approved by the Board or committed to grantees'), FFTC ('when approved and all conditions have been met'), Vanguard (expense when authorized).
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Note 2 Grants (also EV-B-011 (i), EV-B-012 Note 9, EV-B-009 Note 2)

authoritative_findings.claim: A promise to give is an agreement; recognition requires verifiable documentation that the promise was made and received, implying communication to the recipient.

supporting_interpretation: An undisclosed internal approval the sponsor can reverse is an intention, not a promise; communication creates the recipient's expectation and evidence of a promise 'received'.
competing_interpretation: Where the sponsor's governance makes approval binding and payment follows in days, approval itself evidences the obligation (historic 958-720-25-2 text; audited practice).
applicability_to_unbound: Platform default only; the sponsor's policy governs its statements.
business_assumptions: Notices are sent automatically at approval
recommended_answer: Platform default ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee with notice sent atomically at approval, so approval, communication, expense and payable fall in the same period. Whether approval without notice creates a promise is not settled by publicly verifiable authority: treat it as the sponsor's documented accounting policy (SponsorApproval permitted with evidence), not a platform rule.
remaining_uncertainty: Codification text not read; auditor-specific views.
consequences_if_wrong: Small cutoff differences at period end.
alternative_design: Atomic approve-and-notify makes the legal/accounting question moot for nearly all grants at negligible cost; deferred-notice cases (e.g. anonymous or scheduled grants) route through cutoff review.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given approval at time t, when the grant is approved, then a grantee notice is queued at t and its send timestamp recorded.
Given a scheduled grant with notice deferred, when period ends between approval and notice, then it appears on the cutoff report.
external_authorization_required: Sponsor accounting policy accepted by its external auditor.

related_question_answers.answer: Not settled by public authority; superseded 958-720-25-2 recognized at approval or notification and audited sponsors use approval. Record approval, communication, conditions and rescission rights separately; default to communicated-at-approval; allow SponsorApproval under documented policy.
Permit SponsorApproval (evidence-gated), ApprovalCommunicatedToGrantee (default), PaymentReleased (payment as first communication); conditional grants on barrier met.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: States as fact that approval without notice does not create a promise; authority cited as unread secondary knowledge.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Reclassify as interpretation/policy; cite superseded 958-720-25-2 and audited practice as counter-evidence.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Is the DAF component presented as net assets without donor restrictions for every program version, and which account types are agency/pass-through?
original_provisional_answer: Classification by account type: (1) donor-advised funds whose program documents grant the sponsor variance power: contribution revenue, net assets WITHOUT donor restrictions; (2) funds where a nonprofit transfers assets and names itself beneficiary (agency/designated funds) without granting variance power: LIABILITY, not revenue; (3) only gift instruments imposing a time or purpose restriction beyond advisory privileges create net assets WITH donor restrictions. Each program version must store the variance-power clause; missing evidence blocks classification (1).
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: A recipient directed to distribute to a specified unaffiliated beneficiary is a donee (contribution) if the donor explicitly grants variance power - unilateral power to redirect, explicitly referred to in the transfer instrument.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: FAS 136 para 12 (codified in ASC 958-605; Codification paragraph number not verified)

authoritative_findings.claim: A transfer is a liability of the recipient, not a contribution, if the provider retains a unilateral right to redirect, the transfer is revocable/repayable or accompanied by a conditional promise, the provider controls the recipient, or the provider names itself/its affiliate as beneficiary (unless an equity transaction between financially interrelated entities).
Where a nonprofit transfers assets naming itself beneficiary, the community foundation recognizes a liability even though the nonprofit explicitly granted variance power.
Colorado Gives records agency endowments and agency designations as liabilities ($69.7M at 12/31/2025).
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Note 2 Agency Endowments and Designations; Note 7

authoritative_findings.claim: Vanguard classifies its DAFs as net assets without donor restrictions; Fidelity reports $85.8B without and $89M with donor restrictions, including 'accounts with donor-imposed limitations on use' and PIF remainder interests.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Note 2 (and EV-B-008 Note 2 Net Assets With Donor Restrictions)

authoritative_findings.claim: Boston Foundation classifies all funds except perpetual endowments as without donor restrictions because of its variance power - variance power does not remove perpetual time restrictions.
Community foundation National Standards require variance power in fund agreements; hybrid agency funds may split agency vs third-party gifts.

supporting_interpretation: DAF advisory privileges are not donor restrictions; with explicit variance power and sponsor exclusive legal control, DAF contributions are revenue without donor restrictions. Gift instruments imposing time (e.g. perpetual) or purpose restrictions create with-donor-restriction net assets.
competing_interpretation: Some auditors classify certain designated/field-of-interest funds as with donor restrictions despite variance power (Fidelity's with-restriction accounts); pass-through workplace programs where donors can redirect or obtain refunds fail the variance-power test and are liabilities (para 17(a)-(b)).
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound's AccountingTreatment enumeration must be driven by the transfer instrument facts per program version: variance power clause, beneficiary identity (resource provider itself/affiliate), donor redirect/refund rights, time/purpose restrictions, and financial interrelation.
business_assumptions: Program documents are stored per version
Sponsors host agency funds
recommended_answer: Treatments: (1) Contribution without donor restrictions - transfer instrument explicitly grants variance power, no donor redirect/refund right, no time/purpose restriction beyond advisory privileges. (2) Contribution with donor restrictions - instrument imposes time (incl. perpetual) or purpose restriction the sponsor treats as binding (variance power does not remove perpetual endowment restrictions per Boston practice). (3) Liability (agency) - resource provider names itself or affiliate as beneficiary (REGARDLESS of variance power), or provider retains redirect/revocation/refund right, or controls the recipient. (4) Equity transaction - financially interrelated entities naming themselves. Missing variance-power evidence blocks (1).
remaining_uncertainty: Current ASC paragraph numbers for FAS 136 content (958-605-25-24 cross-reference seen in ASU 2018-08; others unverified); sponsor-specific auditor judgments on designated funds.
consequences_if_wrong: Misclassification of revenue vs liability; overstated net assets; Schedule D line errors.
conservative_fallback: Classify as liability any program where variance power evidence is missing or donor retains redirect/refund rights, pending CPA review.
alternative_design: Store transfer-instrument facts (structured clause flags) rather than a free-choice treatment; derive treatment by rule with CPA override and evidence. Low cost; avoids marketing-label misclassification.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given a nonprofit-established agency fund whose agreement grants variance power, when classified, then treatment is Liability.
Given a workplace program allowing donors to redirect or refund, when classified, then treatment is Liability.
Given a DAF program version lacking a stored variance-power clause, when a contribution posts, then posting as unrestricted contribution is blocked.
Given a perpetual endowment gift with variance power, when classified, then treatment is With Donor Restrictions.
external_authorization_required: Sponsor counsel/CPA review of each program's transfer-instrument wording (variance power and beneficiary terms).

related_question_answers.answer: Classify by transfer-instrument facts: explicit variance power and no donor redirect/refund right -> contribution; donor redirect/refund right, provider-named-as-beneficiary or provider control -> liability (FAS 136 paras 12, 17).

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: Says nonprofit-beneficiary agency funds are liabilities 'without granting variance power'; FAS 136 para 17(d) and Example paras 53-56 make them liabilities even when variance power is granted.
Implies variance power alone yields without-donor-restriction classification; Boston keeps perpetual endowments with restrictions and Fidelity has with-restriction accounts.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Variance power makes the sponsor a donee; time/purpose restrictions are separately evaluated.

landscape_update_candidates: Fidelity Charitable FY2025: $89.4M net assets with donor restrictions incl. accounts with donor-imposed limitations on use.
Boston Foundation FY2025: variance power -> all funds except perpetual endowments without restrictions; Board did not use variance power in 2024-2025.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Schedule D line 4 valuation basis and line 3 grant basis (approved vs paid).
original_provisional_answer: Schedule D Part I: line 4 = aggregate fair value of DAF assets at year end, the same measurement as the audited statements; line 3 = all distributions from DAFs including transfers to other funds of the organization, as the instructions require, on the same recognition basis as grant expense (XID-ADV-006). The UNB-XIN-ACC-006 bridge reconciles line 3/4 to GAAP and to fund statements with typed reconciling items (intra-organization transfers, recognition vs payment timing, agency funds, valuation date).
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Line 2: aggregate value of contributions to DAFs during the year; line 3: aggregate value of grants from DAFs, including both grants outside the organization and transfers within the organization; line 4: aggregate value at end of year.
DAFs are not limited to GAAP 'funds'; exceptions include funds distributing only to a single identified organization; column (b) covers other similar funds.
The instructions specify no measurement basis (fair value vs cost, accrual vs paid) for lines 2-4.
Unless instructed otherwise, the return should use the same accounting method the organization uses for its books and records.
Parts XI-XII reconcile audited ASC 958 revenue/expenses to the return.
Schedule D instructions (Rev. 12/2024) are continuous-use for tax year 2024 and later until superseded.

supporting_interpretation: Using the books' method (accrual grant recognition; fair value for investments) for lines 2-4 follows the general accounting-method instruction and makes Schedule D reconcile to audited statements with typed bridge items.
competing_interpretation: Some preparers report line 3 on a paid basis, or exclude intra-organization transfers; agency funds may or may not be DAFs (single-organization funds are excepted) and may belong in column (b) or nowhere.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound produces Schedule D line data and bridge; the sponsor's preparer signs.
business_assumptions: Sponsor books on accrual GAAP
recommended_answer: Line 4 = year-end value of DAF assets on the books' basis (fair value for investments, net of DAF-attributed liabilities such as grants payable when the grant has been expensed); line 3 = grants from DAFs on the same recognition basis as grant expense, plus transfers within the organization (instruction); line 2 = contributions on the GAAP recognition basis. Classify each fund into column (a) DAF, column (b) similar fund, or neither using the statutory definition and exceptions (not GAAP labels). Bridge typed items to GAAP: intra-organization transfers, agency funds, excepted funds, recognition vs paid timing.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether line 4 should be gross assets or net of payables is not stated; preparer practice varies.
consequences_if_wrong: Schedule D inconsistencies; IRS/public scrutiny of DAF payout metrics.
conservative_fallback: Report per preparer instruction with full bridge disclosed in Part XIII.
alternative_design: Provide both gross and net line-4 values and paid vs accrued line-3 values with a preparer-selected basis per tax year; low cost, avoids locking a contested basis.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given $10M DAF grants expensed, of which $0.5M unpaid at year end, and $0.2M transfers between DAFs and other funds, when line 3 is produced on accrual basis, then it equals $10.2M and the bridge shows $0.5M timing vs paid.
Given a fund that distributes only to one identified organization, when Part I is computed, then it is excluded from column (a).
Given a tax-year form revision, when generating, then the instruction version used is recorded.
external_authorization_required: Signed Form 990 by the sponsor officer; preparer acceptance of the line-mapping basis.

related_question_answers.answer: Instructions say only 'aggregate value at the end of the year'; use the books' basis (fair value) and store gross assets, DAF-attributed liabilities and net so the preparer can select; default net of DAF grants payable when grant expense is accrued.

corrections_to_prior_records.issue: Instructions are silent on measurement but not on scope: line 3 expressly includes transfers within the organization, and the general 990 instructions require book-method consistency.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Cite Part I line 3 and General Instructions accounting method.

landscape_update_candidates: Schedule D (Form 990) converted to continuous-use (Rev. 12/2024) for TY2024+.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: UBIT recognition policy (accrue estimate vs recognize on filing) and fund allocation rule.
original_provisional_answer: UBIT is accrued under ASC 740 in the period the unrelated business taxable income is earned (quarterly estimate), trued up on filing Form 990-T. The estimated tax is allocated to the fund(s) that held the income-producing asset in proportion to attributed UBTI, and reduces capacity through a recorded hold at the estimate until the true-up.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: All entities, including tax-exempt NFPs, are subject to ASC 740; UBI recognition is a tax position to evaluate.
NFPs must disclose income tax expense and the nature of activities generating it.
Form 990-T is required at >= $1,000 gross UBI, due the 15th day of the 5th month; estimated tax installments required if expected tax >= $500.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Who Must File; When To File; estimated tax

authoritative_findings.claim: Colorado Gives' audited policy: UBIT 'estimated and recognized as management and general expense in the period the income tax return is filed'.
Fidelity may allocate UBIT arising from contributed property to the Giving Account; Vanguard pays UBIT related to certain illiquid contributions.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: Costs associated with contributions (and EV-B-009 Note 8)

supporting_interpretation: Accrual in the period UBTI is earned follows ASC 740 current-tax principles; allocating to the generating fund mirrors Fidelity's program terms; a capacity hold prevents granting tax money.
competing_interpretation: Where UBIT is immaterial, audited practice (Colorado Gives) recognizes it when the return is filed; auditors accept this on materiality grounds.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound should always place the capacity hold at fund level (risk control) and let the sponsor's policy choose GL timing (accrual default; filing basis permitted if CPA-documented as immaterial).
business_assumptions: UBTI sources identifiable per fund (S-corp, K-1, debt-financed)
Program terms permit charging tax to the fund
recommended_answer: Default: accrue estimated UBIT in the period earned (quarterly estimates aligned with 990-T installments), true-up on filing, allocate to generating funds pro rata to attributed UBTI where program terms allow, and hold that capacity until true-up. Permit filing-basis GL recognition only under a documented sponsor policy (immateriality), while keeping the fund-level capacity hold.
remaining_uncertainty: Codification paragraphs not read; allocation of shared deductions/specific deduction across funds is a tax method choice.
consequences_if_wrong: Granting money owed as tax; misallocated tax across donors.
conservative_fallback: Capacity hold at estimate regardless of GL policy.
alternative_design: Refuse UBTI-generating assets (no S-corp/K-1 acceptance): eliminates exposure but loses complex-asset gifts (Fidelity reports $1.75B private equity securities contributed assets). Recommended: accept with hold and allocation.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given policy Accrue, when Q2 closes with $20,000 UBTI attributed to fund F, then an estimated tax accrual posts in Q2 allocated to F and F's capacity is held.
Given policy FilingBasis, when Q2 closes, then no GL accrual posts but F's capacity hold is still placed.
Given expected annual tax >= $500, when quarter installment dates approach, then an estimated-payment task is created.
external_authorization_required: Sponsor program terms permitting charge of UBIT to the fund; sponsor tax preparer's allocation method.

related_question_answers.answer: ASC 740 applies; default accrual with true-up; filing-basis recognition seen in audited practice (Colorado Gives) acceptable only under documented immateriality policy; capacity hold always.

corrections_to_prior_records.record_or_artifact: XID-INV-006 decision_outcome.rationale 'GAAP requires accrual of income tax'
corrections_to_prior_records.issue: True in principle but audited practice shows filing-basis recognition (Colorado Gives FY2025) accepted when immaterial.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Make GL timing a policy with accrual default; keep capacity hold unconditional.

landscape_update_candidates: Colorado Gives FY2025 recognizes UBIT in the period the return is filed.
Fidelity Charitable program terms allocate UBIT from contributed property to the Giving Account.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Relationship between management ABC and Form 990 functional expense allocation
original_provisional_answer: Management activity-based costing and the GAAP/Form 990 functional expense allocation use the same activity dataset with two separately governed mappings. The functional mapping is accounting policy, approved annually by the controller and external CPA, and is the only one that reaches financial statements. The management mapping never posts.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: All NFPs must present expenses by both function and nature in one location, and disclose methods used to allocate costs among program and support functions.

Form 990 Part IX uses the organization's normal accounting method; if the accounting system does not allocate expenses, any reasonable allocation method may be used, reported accurately and documented.
Return should generally use the same accounting method as the books.
No authority governs internal management activity-based costing; it is management information.

supporting_interpretation: One activity dataset, two governed mappings: the functional mapping is accounting policy feeding GAAP and Part IX; the ABC mapping never posts.
competing_interpretation: Using one mapping for both reduces cost but lets management changes alter reported functional expenses.
applicability_to_unbound: Applies to sponsor operating expenses and Unbound's cost-attribution engine.
business_assumptions: Time/activity data is captured
recommended_answer: Adopt as decided, with one correction: the functional allocation method is management's accounting policy (controller/CFO approves annually and documents it); the external auditor audits it and the preparer uses it for Part IX - the CPA does not 'approve' it.
remaining_uncertainty: Joint-cost allocation (958-720-45-28 et seq.) not researched.
consequences_if_wrong: Functional expense misstatement; Part IX/GAAP mismatch.
conservative_fallback: Single functional mapping only; ABC derived as non-posting view.
alternative_design: Independent datasets (higher cost, reconciliation burden) vs shared dataset (recommended).
required_acceptance_criteria: Given a management ABC mapping change, when statements regenerate, then functional expense totals are unchanged.
Given the functional mapping version v approved by the controller, when Part IX is produced, then it uses v and the allocation-method disclosure text is generated.

corrections_to_prior_records.record_or_artifact: XID-ECO-005 confirmation_required 'External CPA approves the functional mapping annually'
corrections_to_prior_records.issue: No requirement for CPA approval; allocation is management's policy, audited by the auditor.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Controller/CFO approves; auditor reviews in audit.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Default treatment for postings whose effective date falls in a hard-closed period: current-period prior-period adjustment, reopen, or restatement, and the materiality threshold for each
original_provisional_answer: A posting whose effective date falls in a hard-closed period posts in the current open period with relates_to_period and a correction class. If the affected statements have not been issued, see XID-ADV-005. If they have been issued: immaterial → current-period correction with disclosure ('little r' revision where comparatives shown); material → formal restatement of comparatives, with originally issued statements preserved. A hard-closed period is reopened only before issuance and only with controller + CFO approval. Materiality is set annually by the CFO with the auditor (illustrative quantitative default 0.5% of total net assets or 5% of the change in net assets, whichever is lower, plus qualitative factors). Donor-facing fund statements already issued are always corrected by an adjustment line with explanation on the next statement, and an amended statement is issued whenever an acknowledgment or a tax-relevant figure changes.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: An error in prior-period statements discovered after issuance is reported as a prior-period adjustment by restating prior statements (cumulative effect to opening net assets of the first period presented; period-specific effects corrected) with disclosure.
authoritative_findings.pinpoint: FAS 154 paras 25-26 (codified ASC 250-10-45-23 and 250-10-50-7; paragraph mapping not verified)

authoritative_findings.claim: Materiality cannot rest exclusively on a numerical threshold; qualitative factors apply.
Auditor planning materiality example for NFPs is 1% of total revenue or expenses, adjustable by judgment.
Concepts Statement 8 Ch.3 (as amended 2018) treats materiality as entity-specific; FASB sets no uniform threshold (secondary, not fetched).
The 'little r' revision approach is SEC staff practice (SAB 108) and was not verified here for NFPs.

supporting_interpretation: Posting late items in the open period with relates_to_period preserves closed-period immutability; restatement only when material to issued statements follows ASC 250.
competing_interpretation: Some sponsors prefer reopening before issuance; an immaterial error that would be material if corrected in the current period requires revision of comparatives.
applicability_to_unbound: Unbound implements routing, evidence and approvals; materiality is a sponsor/auditor judgment input, not a platform constant.
business_assumptions: Sponsor has CFO and auditor
Donor statements issued periodically
recommended_answer: Keep: effective date and posting period stored separately; post in current open period with relates_to_period and correction class; before issuance see XID-ADV-005; after issuance, CFO determines materiality (with auditor input) - material: restate comparatives and preserve originally issued statements; immaterial: correct in current period, and revise comparatives if correcting currently would itself be material. Remove the '0.5% of net assets or 5% of change' default or label it 'illustrative, non-authoritative'; require a recorded qualitative assessment. Controller approval matrix risk-based (amount, cumulative, unusual, related-party). Donor statements: adjustment line on next statement; amended acknowledgment whenever an acknowledged amount or date changes.
remaining_uncertainty: Codification text not read; AU-C 320 text not fetched.
consequences_if_wrong: Failure to restate when required or unnecessary restatements.
conservative_fallback: Escalate any correction to issued periods to CFO with auditor consultation before posting.
alternative_design: (a) Always reopen: breaks immutability. (b) Current-period posting with relates_to_period (recommended). (c) Separate restatement ledger version: higher build cost, cleanest comparatives.
required_acceptance_criteria: Given a hard-closed issued period and a correction, when posted, then it lands in the open period with relates_to_period and correction class, and the original issued statement version is retained.
Given a correction classified Material by the CFO, when statements regenerate, then restated comparatives and disclosure fields are produced.
Given no recorded qualitative materiality assessment, when classifying, then classification cannot complete.

related_question_answers.answer: No authoritative threshold; use a risk-based approval matrix (amount, cumulative, unusual, related-party) set by the CFO; numeric values are sponsor policy.

corrections_to_prior_records.record_or_artifact: XID-EVA-002 decision_outcome illustrative default '0.5% of total net assets or 5% of the change in net assets'
corrections_to_prior_records.issue: No authoritative basis; SAB 99 rejects exclusive numerical thresholds and auditor examples use other benchmarks (1% revenue/expenses for NFPs).
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Delete or label as non-authoritative illustration; require qualitative assessment.

exact_question: Confirm provisional decision: Routing of prior-year adjustments discovered during and after the audit (AuditAdjustment period vs PriorPeriodAdjustment).
original_provisional_answer: Before the audited statements are issued, adjustments found during the audit post in a soft-closed AuditAdjustment period (period 13) and accept only journals linked to an AuditFinding. After issuance, the XID-EVA-002 route applies.
jurisdiction: United States (federal tax law; US GAAP for not-for-profit entities)

authoritative_findings.claim: Entities that are not public entities evaluate subsequent events through the date statements are 'available to be issued' (complete and all approvals obtained); public entities, which include conduit bond obligors, use the issued date.
Recognized subsequent events providing evidence about balance-sheet-date conditions adjust the statements.
Errors found after issuance require restatement (if material).
Fidelity Charitable evaluated subsequent events through the available-to-be-issued date (Oct 29, 2025).

supporting_interpretation: Before the statements are available to be issued, audit adjustments are simply corrections of draft statements; a controlled period-13 that accepts only finding-linked journals preserves the closed period 12 and gives an audit trail.
competing_interpretation: Some ERPs reopen period 12; others post audit adjustments as top-side entries outside the ledger.
applicability_to_unbound: Boundary event must be configurable per sponsor (available-to-be-issued vs issued) because some sponsors are conduit bond obligors.
business_assumptions: Sponsor audit cycle with management representation date
recommended_answer: Adopt period 13 (AuditAdjustment) accepting only AuditFinding-linked journals until the statements are available to be issued (non-public NFPs) or issued (public entities incl. conduit bond obligors); thereafter route per XID-EVA-002. Record the boundary date and basis per fiscal year.
remaining_uncertainty: Auditor preference for top-side vs ledger entries.
consequences_if_wrong: Adjustments posted into wrong period or after issuance without restatement analysis.
conservative_fallback: Lock period 13 at report date and require CFO approval for any later entry.
alternative_design: Reopen period 12 (simpler, loses immutability) vs period 13 (recommended) vs top-side only (loses ledger traceability).
required_acceptance_criteria: Given period 13 open, when a journal without an AuditFinding link is submitted, then it is rejected.
Given sponsor flagged conduit bond obligor, when boundary is computed, then the issued date is used; otherwise available-to-be-issued date.
Given boundary passed, when an adjustment is submitted, then it routes to the XID-EVA-002 flow.

corrections_to_prior_records.record_or_artifact: XID-ADV-005 decision_outcome 'boundary set at issuance date'
corrections_to_prior_records.issue: For non-public NFPs ASC 855 uses the available-to-be-issued date (Fidelity practice); 'issued' applies to public entities including conduit bond obligors.
corrections_to_prior_records.correction: Make boundary per sponsor: available-to-be-issued (default) or issued (public/conduit).
